justice: Most of the visible right-of-way is allocated to multiple wide motor-vehicle lanes, while no clear sidewalk is visible on either side of the road.
There is no visible marked pedestrian crossing, curb ramp, or tactile paving, so access appears to favor drivers over people walking or using mobility aids.
The landscaped median and roadside greenery improve visual quality, but they do not visibly provide inclusive travel space for non-motorized users.
Streetlights are provided along the corridor, showing some public investment, yet the absence of visible pedestrian or bicycle facilities suggests uneven distribution of street assets.
safety: Fresh lane markings, a wide carriageway, and a planted median help organize vehicle movement and reduce head-on conflict.
Streetlights line both sides of the road, which can support nighttime visibility and traffic safety.
The road geometry is broad and open, which improves forward sight distance for drivers.
However, the high-speed design character, long uninterrupted lanes, and lack of visible crosswalks or refuge points reduce safety for pedestrians and cyclists.
livability: The corridor appears low-density and largely inactive, with very limited visible shops, services, or street-level destinations.
Large expanses of asphalt and open verge create a transport corridor rather than a socially vibrant public street.
Some housing is visible in the distance on the left, but buildings are set far back and do not contribute much active frontage.
Trees and planted medians add environmental quality, yet there are no visible benches, gathering spaces, or transit stops to support everyday street life.
sustainability: The planted median, roadside grass, and tree rows provide some green infrastructure and ecological value compared with a fully paved corridor.
The streetlights and orderly road design suggest formal infrastructure that may support durable long-term operation.
No dedicated bus stop, bike lane, or other visible low-carbon mobility facility is apparent in the scene.
The very wide motor-vehicle-oriented roadway likely encourages car dependence, limiting overall transport sustainability.
aesthetics: The newly paved road surface, clean lane markings, and orderly streetlight rhythm create a neat and coherent visual appearance.
Green median planting and tree lines on the right soften the roadway and improve scenic quality.
The broad sky view and uncluttered corridor give the scene an open and spacious character.
At the same time, the environment is visually monotonous because of the long expanse of asphalt and limited architectural frontage.
comfort: Thermal comfort is mixed: there are trees and planting strips, but the roadway itself is highly exposed to direct sun with little visible shade over travel space.
Physical comfort for pedestrians is poor because no clear sidewalk, seating, or sheltered waiting area is visible.
Psychological comfort for non-drivers is limited by the wide, fast-looking road profile and the lack of protected walking or cycling space.
For drivers, the smooth pavement and generous lane width provide comfortable movement and low immediate congestion.
walkability: No continuous sidewalk is clearly visible along the road, making basic pedestrian movement difficult.
There are no visible marked crossings, pedestrian refuge islands, or curb ramps to support safe route continuity.
The long block structure and road width imply extended crossing distances and low convenience for people on foot.
Although roadside greenery improves the visual environment, the corridor remains strongly vehicle-oriented rather than walk-oriented.
bikeability: No dedicated bike lane, painted cycle marking, or physically protected cycling space is visible.
The wide, fast-looking motor-traffic lanes would likely make on-road cycling stressful for most users.
There is no visible bicycle parking, bike signal, or intersection treatment that would support convenient cycling.
The smooth pavement is a positive feature for riding quality, but the lack of separation from traffic keeps overall bikeability low.
